days.headline: Day after Munich
days.summary: Rested as planned, the day after Munich.
learn: Rest as planned. Walks don't need to be logged.

days.headline: Full rest
learn: Rest as planned, two days after the marathon.

days.headline: Optional swim, not recorded
days.summary: No swim in Strava. It was optional, so nothing is lost. If you swam without the watch, add it so the week total is right.
learn: This session was optional, so skipping it costs nothing. If you did swim without the watch, add it so the week total is right.

days.headline: Recovery run moved to Friday
days.summary: Not run today. You ran this recovery run on Friday instead: 4.38 km at 6:00 /km.
learn: No run recorded today. It shows up on Friday, so the plan counts it as moved, not missed.
Note why it moved. After a few weeks the reasons show a pattern: meetings, weather, fatigue.

days.headline: Thursday's run, done a day late
days.summary: Planned rest day. You ran Thursday's recovery run here instead. Km 1 heart rate read 88 bpm (sensor still locking on), so the real average is about 132, not 122. Km 3–4 went over the 130 cap.

activity.hrNote: Km 1 read 88 bpm while the sensor locked on; the real average is about 132.

learn: Km 1 averaged 88 bpm while pace was normal: the sensor was still locking on. The real average is closer to 132, so treat 122 as a reading error, not a win.
Km 3–4 were over the cap at an even 5:52–5:57 /km. Cap creep starts in the second half, so slow down before it, not after.
Moving the run kept the week's volume, but it made Friday–Saturday back-to-back. That's fine in a recovery week; in the build, move rest days, not runs.

days.headline: Recovery run, a little too quick
days.summary: Run on the planned day, close to the planned distance, but 17 s/km quicker than needed. Heart rate sat 4–6 bpm over the 130 cap from km 2 on: about 6:00 /km is your under-130 pace for now.
learn: Heart rate sat 4–6 bpm over the 130 cap from km 2 on, at 5:25–5:47 /km. Friday, at about 5:55 /km, km 2 stayed at 129. For now, your under-130 pace is about 6:00 /km or slower.
Two Strava segment PRs on a recovery run is a warning sign: segments pull the pace up. Run the loop the other way round, or hide pace and watch only heart rate.
Average heart rate sat in the 130–140 band, one band above the cap. The plan's 130 is strict on purpose this week: muscle damage, not fitness, is the limit.

days.headline: Recovery run, kept under the cap
days.summary: Planned 30 min recovery run, done on the day: 4.84 km in 30:00 at about 6:12 /km. Average 125 bpm, highest km lap 128, so every lap stayed under the 130 cap.
learn: Laps ran 6:20, 5:48, 6:08 and 6:19 /km at 120–128 bpm, all under the 130 cap. About 6:10 /km or slower keeps you in the <130 band for now.
Km 2 was the quickest at 5:48 /km, on a slight downhill, and heart rate rose to 126. Let a downhill pull the pace up and you start eating into the cap.
Max heart rate 137 came on km 4, the climb (9 m gain). Tuesday's easy run has a 140 cap, but keep the same patience on hills.

days.headline: Easy swim, not recorded
days.summary: No swim in Strava. If you swam without the watch, it can be added so the week total is right.
learn: Pool sessions only show up here if the watch recorded them. If you swam off-watch, add it.

days.headline: Easy run, inside the 140 cap
days.summary: Planned 30 min easy run, done on the day: 5.14 km in 30:14 at about 5:53 /km. Average 133 bpm against the 140 cap; the peak was 145 on the bridge climbs.
learn: Average 133 bpm sat in the 130–140 band, inside the 140 cap, at about 5:53 /km. That is the right effort for this run.
Max 145 came on the climbs: 'Over the bridges back' and '3 Brücken Sprint raus' averaged 138–139. The plan calls 140 a hard ceiling, so walk the hill rather than cross it.
Strava recorded one 5.1 km lap, so there is no per-km check. Set the watch to auto-lap every km to see where heart rate drifts.

days.headline: Recovery run, under the cap
days.summary: Planned 4.5 km recovery run, done on the day in the evening: 4.68 km in 27:24 at about 5:51 /km. Average 121 bpm and max 138, so the run stayed inside the 130 cap on average. The home strength session isn't in Strava; it can be added if done off-watch.
learn: Average 121 bpm at about 5:51 /km, well under the 130 cap. Max 138 came on the climbs, so it briefly crossed the cap there.
Strava recorded one 4.5 km lap, so there is no per-km check against the cap. Set the watch to auto-lap every km.
Segments in the first 2 km read 87–104 bpm, which looks like slow sensor lock-on. The real average is probably a few bpm above 121, still inside the <130 band.

days.headline: Easy run moved to Friday
days.summary: Planned 6.5 km easy run. Nothing recorded on the day; you ran an easy 5.49 km on Friday's rest day instead.
learn: The run moved a day rather than being skipped, which is fine this week. Keep the next rest day free of running.

days.headline: Thursday's easy run, done on the rest day
days.summary: Planned rest day. You ran Thursday's easy run here: 5.49 km in 31:31 at about 5:45 /km, shorter than the 6.5 km planned but well inside the 45 min stop-by. Heart rate reads low after km 2 (sensor dropout), so the average of 105 is not real.

activity.hrNote: Km 3 to the end read 74–102 bpm, clearly a sensor dropout; only km 1–2 (126 and 136 bpm) are trustworthy.

learn: Km 1 and 2 ran 5:36 and 5:45 /km at 126 and 136 bpm, inside the 140 cap; the rest of the heart rate trace is unusable.
Check the strap or watch fit before the next run so the cap can be checked over the whole distance.

days.headline: Easy run, longer than planned and over the cap late
days.summary: Planned 5.5 km easy run with strides (cap 140). Done on the day in the evening: 6.97 km in 38:19 at about 5:30 /km. Average 138 bpm, but the last 2.7 km averaged 144 and the run peaked at 157, over the 140 cap. It ran about 1.5 km past the plan, still inside the 40 min stop-by.
learn: The first 2.8 km ran at 5:25 /km and 131 bpm, right in the easy range. The final 2.7 km ran 5:36 /km at 144 bpm, over the 140 cap: finish as relaxed as you start.
Heart rate ran 139–147 through the stride block. Strides may go above the cap, but let it settle back under 140 between them.
Max 157 landed in the last section, in the 155–LT band. On an easy day, walk or ease off as soon as the watch reads 140.

days.headline: Easy run not recorded
days.summary: Planned 8 km easy run (stop by 55 min). Nothing in Strava that day or within two days that matches it, so it counts as missed. If you ran off-watch, it can be added.
learn: The 8 km run was the week's longest. Monday's run was 4.15 km, so the week is about 4 km short of the long-run plan; don't make it up in one go.
If a run is skipped, drop it rather than stacking it onto the next day: the plan's 140 cap matters more than the km.

days.headline: Easy run, short of the plan, inside the cap
days.summary: Planned 6.5 km easy run with strides (cap 140). Done on the day in the evening: 4.15 km in 23:20 at about 5:37 /km. Average 136 bpm, peak 149. It ended about 2.3 km short of the plan and well before the 40 min mark.
learn: Average 136 bpm sat in the 130–140 band, under the 140 cap, at about 5:37 /km. Max 149 reached the 140–155 band, probably on the strides.
Strava recorded one 4.15 km lap, so there is no per-km check against the cap. Set the watch to auto-lap every km.
The run stopped at 23 minutes against about 40 planned. If it was fatigue, the shorter run is the right call; note the reason so a pattern shows.

days.headline: Easy run, average inside the cap, one spike to 160
days.summary: Planned 6.5 km easy run (cap 140). Done on the day in the morning: 4.86 km in 25:54 at about 5:20 /km. Average 137 bpm, inside the 140 cap, but the peak was 160. It ended about 1.6 km short of the plan and well before the 45 min stop-by. The home strength session isn't in Strava; it can be added if done off-watch.
learn: Average 137 bpm sat in the 130–140 band, under the 140 cap, but at 5:20 /km it is your quickest easy run this week (Monday was 5:37, Saturday 5:30). The pace came from effort, not from a lower heart rate.
Max 160 landed in the 155–LT band. The climb segments read 142 bpm ('Wiesen North End', 'behind the Girl'), so the spike was probably a short hill push: walk it once the watch reads 140.
Strava recorded one 4.85 km lap, so there is no per-km check against the cap. Set the watch to auto-lap every km.
